 Ramos and those 11.3 km covered per match that say a lot about his poor feeling for goal at Milan
 Serie A 
 Calcio 
 Among the most generous athletically - 124.6 kilometres in the first eleven matchdays -, but the Portuguese's attacking output remains below expectations. One goal every 62 km...
 Andrea Ramazzotti 
 14 november (updated at 18:29) - MILANO 
 English 
 Italiano 
 Deutsch 
 Choose Gazzetta as your preferred source on Google 
 One goal every… 62 kilometres covered. To tell the story of Gonçalo Ramos's difficult start to the season in front of goal, you only need to put a few numbers together. The Portuguese has scored two goals in the first eleven Serie A matchdays and has covered 124.6 kilometres. Milan signed him from PSG at the end of June for €70 million plus bonuses. With ancillary costs included, the figure recorded in the accounts is €73.1 million. Since then, Ramos has started every league match and has played 981 minutes out of 990, excluding stoppage time. He runs a lot to lead the press and disrupt the opposition playmaker whenever Milan lose possession. It is work that often takes him far from goal and can cost him some composure when finishing. What is certain is that, with an average of 11.3 kilometres per match, he is the forward who has covered... the most ground in Serie A. "I have no intention of saying that Ramos needs to run less, I will never say that about a player," Rubén Amorim explained to DAZN. The manager highlighted the Portuguese's contribution to the team's goals and said he is convinced that, by continuing to work like this, he will get back among the goals. 
 only two ahead
—   After eleven matchdays, only two players in the whole of Serie A have covered more kilometres than Ramos, both midfielders. They are Lewis Ferguson of Bologna, first with 136.76 kilometres, and Ederson of Atalanta, second with 126.12. Behind the Portuguese are Pierre Kalulu, the Juventus defender, on 123.72 kilometres, and Jesper Karlström, the Udinese midfielder, on 123.54. Ramos's generosity is invaluable to the Rossoneri's pressing, but more was expected in front of goal from a centre-forward of his calibre. So far he has scored one goal every 491 minutes. Of his 26 shots in the league, half came in the opening two matchdays, five against Torino and eight against Venezia. Against Juventus, Lecce, Bologna and Inter, on the other hand, he never managed a shot, although against the Salentini he provided an assist. He is currently away on Nations League duty with Portugal. After Tuesday's clash against Wales, he will return to focus on Milan, who also need his goals to climb the table. Not just his running...
